items.title: Library supplement: Angular geometry on the actual unit sphere

items.statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure, and let S be its literal unit-norm subtype. The actual angular cost c(u,v)=arccos(inner(u,v)) is jointly continuous and measurable on S×S. For every pair it lies between zero and pi, equals Mathlib's unoriented vector angle, dominates the ambient chord norm, vanishes exactly on the diagonal, and is symmetric. It satisfies the triangle inequality. These are explicit properties of the angular cost; no inherited chord-distance instance is replaced, no path-length geodesic-distance identification or Wasserstein theorem is included, and no sphere nonemptiness or positive dimension is assumed.
assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel measurable structure.
S is exactly the unit-norm subtype and c(u,v)=arccos(inner(u,v)). Neither positive dimension nor a point of S is assumed.

formulae.label: Angular geometry on the actual unit sphere
formulae.tex: c(u,v)=\arccos\langle u,v\rangle,\quad 0\le c\le\pi,\quad \|u-v\|\le c(u,v),\quad c(u,w)\le c(u,v)+c(v,w).

obligations.label: Angular geometry on the actual unit sphere

bindings.boundary: Explicit cost properties only. The inherited subtype distance is still the ambient chord distance; no metric instance is changed.; No intrinsic path-length identity, installed manifold API, Wasserstein theorem or statistical model is certified. In dimension one the two-point sphere has finite angular cost but no internal path between its two points.

items.statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel measurable structure and H a complete real inner-product normed space. Let F:E→H have actual ambient Frechet derivative D(w):E→H for every w. Assume nonnegative M1,M2, an operator bound norm(D(w))<=M1 on the closed unit ball and an operator-Lipschitz bound norm(D(w)-D(u))<=M2 norm(w-u) there. Fix y in H. On the actual unit-norm subtype S define K(w)=F(w), angular cost c(u,v)=arccos(inner(u,v)), the actual Bochner mean m(mu)=integral K dmu, V_mu(w)=2 inner(m(mu)-y,F(w)), and G_mu(w)=2P_w D(w)^*(m(mu)-y) with the explicit projection P_w z=z−⟨z,w⟩w, which projects onto w-perpendicular when norm(w)=1. Let Q(mu,nu) be the literal extended nonnegative infimum of the quadratic angular cost over all actual couplings. There exist C1,C2>0, independent of probability laws and unit weights, such that for every actual parameter probability K is integrable, V_mu has the displayed ambient gradient 2D(w)^*(m(mu)-y) at every ambient w, and its projected G_mu is tangent and uniformly bounded by C1 at every unit weight. For every two actual parameter probabilities Q is finite and norm(G_mu(w)-G_nu(u))<=C2*(sqrt(Q).toReal+c(w,u)). Feature boundedness, strong measurability, feature Lipschitz control and residual budgets are derived inside the proof rather than assumed; the returned conclusions are feature integrability, actual ambient gradient, tangency/uniform bound, finite transport cost and the joint sensitivity estimate. The constants may depend on the displayed feature/derivative data, E,H and y. This is a generic feature-law theorem, not a concrete Gaussian scalar-data potential, installed manifold-gradient/Wasserstein API or intrinsic path-length theorem.
assumptions: E is finite-dimensional real Hilbert with Borel structure; H is a complete real inner-product normed space, with no separability assumption.
F:E→H has actual full ambient Frechet derivative D(w) at every w. M1,M2≥0 bound the derivative operator norm and its operator Lipschitz increment on the closed unit ball.
y is fixed. S is the literal unit-norm subtype; m is the actual Bochner integral, c the literal arccos cost, and Q the infimum of angular squared cost over all actual couplings.

formulae.label: Uniform gradients of quadratic feature-law potentials
formulae.tex: P_wz=z-\langle z,w\rangle w,\quad V_\mu(w)=2\langle m_\mu-y,F(w)\rangle,\quad G_\mu(w)=2P_wD(w)^*(m_\mu-y),\quad \|G_\mu(w)-G_\nu(u)\|\le C_2\bigl(Q(\mu,\nu)^{1/2}+c(w,u)\bigr).

obligations.label: Uniform gradients of quadratic feature-law potentials

bindings.boundary: F and D plus their actual derivative/operator bounds remain explicit generic inputs. A specific model must produce them and identify its literal scalar potential with this Hilbert potential.; Angular all-coupling cost, tangent projection and actual ambient gradient are explicit. Identification with a chosen Riemannian-gradient/Wasserstein API or intrinsic path-length convention remains separate.; Auxiliary feature bounds, strong measurability and residual estimates are derived internally; they are not separately returned conjuncts. Constants may depend on E,H,F,D,M1,M2,y.
